status: captured (home + 5 subpages), judged by 2 combined AI jurors from evidence packs; owner scores pending

jury.note: two combined jurors instead of five (cost test): 87k + 94k tokens

business.what: Group tennis classes for kids (from age 2-3) and adults plus private lessons, at City of Vancouver community centres and Park Board courts; registration and payment hand off to the city's ActiveNet system (inference).
business.action_that_pays: REGISTER per class on /classes; 'Buy on ActiveNet' for private lessons ($28.50-$100 per person per lesson)

claims.claim: Tennis balls that wobble; pictures cut the frame and come out of it
claims.evidence: Frame-break: drawn racquets and balls overlap the photo frames; the photos themselves stay inside. Measured live: the hero ball bounces (translateY about -21 to -27px) and three round icons spin continuously.

claims.claim: Icons a little classic but comfortable to read
claims.evidence: Functional icons are simple consistent glyphs (plus in a yellow circle, pin, external-link arrow, numbered discs); the 'classic' feel belongs to the sticker-style illustrations (megaphone ATTENTION, peace hand, badge).

claims.claim: Animated text on a circular / wavy shape is unique
claims.evidence: Text-on-path ribbon with the method slogan ('The pathway is the progression...') and a round EST 2012 badge. A common pattern; its value is that it repeats the message.

claims.claim: Map with custom objects is fun
claims.evidence: Custom map markers (smiling tennis balls) on a stylised, likely static map next to a list of 8 centres; pins are unlabelled and not shown to be interactive.
The spinning circles are decorative loops, not micro-interactions. The real micro-interaction, measured: buttons lose their offset shadow on hover, a 'press' effect.

library_candidates: Palette from the sport: optic yellow, court green, cream
Frame-breaking drawn objects over real photos: brand voice without a new shoot
Pill buttons with a hard offset shadow that 'press' on hover, site-wide
Text-on-path ribbon that carries the method's slogan as a divider
Themed map markers (tennis balls) beside a list of locations
Sticker-style illustrations (megaphone, peace hand, badge) as pauses between sections
Class cards with level, venue, day/time, sessions, 'N spots left', REGISTER with an external-link icon, plus filters
Waitlist form ('notify me when registration opens') when a class is full
Price grid by group size x number of lessons with a 'best value' column
Level ladders with entry criteria so people place themselves
avoid: Motion that ignores reduced motion and 58 endless loops with no pause
White text on #00ce7d level tags (2.07:1) and orange scarcity text (3.42:1)
No price for group classes anywhere; payment split across two systems
Hero trust built on 'Vancouver's best' and an unsourced '10,000 students' while checkable proof sits on About

owner_taste_signal: Fifth batch: the owner again likes expressive, playful, subject-made visuals (balls, stickers, wavy text) and motion; again the strongest site for craft is weaker on business (no group price). The owner proposed five standards; evaluated in the review.
